arabic_anchors: ممَّا قصدنا له قوله عزوجل: ﴿بِسْمِ ٱللهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيـمِ﴾
ويُسألُ عن التكرير في قوله عزوجل: ﴿الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيـمِ﴾
ورَوَى مطرٌ عن قتادة في قوله: ﴿بِسْمِ ٱللهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيـمِ﴾ قال: مَدَح نفسَهُ
evidence.quran_alignment: The complete entry opens and closes on the basmala of canonical 1:1. Between them it explains ba, ism derivations, Allah's form, and the paired mercy names, their force/order, and their function as praise. All full 1:1-3 packet context was read. The extended treatment of al-Rahman/al-Rahim belongs to the explicitly framed basmala; repetition of those words at 1:3 alone does not require another target.
evidence.translation_alignment: Full TR/EN preserve the entire sequence, both etymology positions, lakinna comparison, poem, all reported views of the mercy names, and the closing Qatada and Abu al-'Abbas remarks. They follow this source's mapping; notes and translation choices do not substitute another entry.
evidence.excluded_as_extra_targets: Fetched and read full canonical 18:38. The cited لَّٰكِنَّاْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي, its expansion لَكِنْ أَنَا, and al-Hasan's reading are a short phonological comparison introduced by كما while explaining loss of hamza and assimilation in Allah. They remain an illustrative cross-reference, not an additional substantive target. The poem, al-nas/unās example and Jarir adjective example are likewise explanatory witnesses.

arabic_anchors: قولُه تعالى: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ﴾ الفرقُ بين الحمد والشكر
قولك: الحمدُ للهِ مَخْرجُهُ في الاعراب، مَخْرج قولك: المالُ لزيدٍ
evidence.quran_alignment: The complete passage is divided into al-hamdu lillah and Rabb al-'alamin, exactly the two constituents of canonical 1:2. It explains hamd versus shukr, nominative/accusative force, praise/request and divine self-praise, then Rabb derivation and interpretations/derivation of 'alamin. Full 1:1-4 packet context confirms the target.
evidence.translation_alignment: Read complete Turkish and English from hamd/shukr through the closing Creator/Disposer explanation. Both preserve the same two verse sections, hadith and poems, Ibn Kaysan's discussion, and the reported interpretations of worlds. No mapping divergence found.
evidence.excluded_as_extra_targets: The hadith, المال لزيد, human self-praise illustrations, and two poetic witnesses support 1:2's lexical and rhetorical explanation; none is an independent Qur'anic target or surah introduction.
evidence.digital_source: https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/2 full substantive passage opened and checked from قوله تعالى الحمد لله through فالعالم دال على أن له خالقا ومدبرا.

source_limits: Original digital passage checked; no printed facsimile inspected. Historical/lexical reports and their translation are assessed for association only and remain frozen.

arabic_anchors: قوله تعالى: ﴿مَلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ﴾ ويُقْرأ ﴿مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ﴾
فإن قيل: لم خُصَّت القيامة بهذا؟
evidence.quran_alignment: Full AR/TR/EN and 1:2-6 context read. The entry's two linked topics are Malik/Malik readings and the meaning of yawm al-din, followed by why the Day is singled out for divine sovereignty. Those directly explain full canonical 1:4 مَـٰلِكِ يَوْمِ ٱلدِّينِ.
evidence.translation_alignment: TR and EN preserve the competing readings, Abu Hatim's argument and rebuttal, entire isnad, reckoning/requital glosses, din's other senses and final resurrection explanation. English's note on al-Suddi's name concerns source wording and does not shift association.
evidence.excluded_as_extra_targets: Full 40:16 was separately retrieved and read. لِمَنِ الْمُلْكُ الْيَوْمَ is explicitly adduced with واحتجوا as lexical evidence for the Malik reading of 1:4; the brief mulk/milk distinction supports that argument. It is an illustrative cross-reference, not an independently developed 40:16 exposition. The customary-din poem is also a lexical witness.
evidence.digital_source: https://tafsir.app/nahaas-meanings/1/4 opened and substantive passage checked in full, including opening variant readings and the last sentence returning all authority to Allah on the Resurrection.

arabic_anchors: قوله تعالى: ﴿إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ﴾ ولم يقل «نَعْبُدكَ» لأن هذا أوكدُ
والعبادة في اللغة: الطَّاعة مع تذلُّل وخضوع
وفي الكلام حذفٌ والمعنى: وإياكَ نستعين على ذلك
evidence.quran_alignment: Full Arabic, Turkish, English and packet 1:3-7 context read. The opening explains fronting of iyyaka and the lexical meaning of worship; the second section explains its repetition, second-person address, and the omitted complement of nasta'in. These are substantive explanations of both halves of canonical 1:5.
evidence.translation_alignment: Both complete translations reproduce the same fronting/worship discussion, both lexical poems, second iyyaka emphasis, al-A'sha illustration, three Qur'anic citations about person shifts, and the final omitted complement. They follow the same source unit.
evidence.excluded_as_extra_targets: Retrieved and read full canonical 76:21-22 and 10:22. The cited portions are presented exclusively as witnesses for switches between third person and address, alongside poetry; no distinct thematic or syntactic exposition of those verses is developed. They are not additional mapping targets. The beaten-road phrase is a lexical illustration of worship, not commentary on 1:6.

arabic_anchors: وأصلُ هذا كله: أرشد، والمعنى: أرشدنا إلى الصراط المستقيم
evidence.quran_alignment: Complete AR/TR/EN and 1:4-7 context read. The passage explains why already-guided speakers ask ihdina, distinguishes hadā's senses, returns explicitly to the meaning of ihdina al-sirat al-mustaqim, and gives Book/Islam interpretations of the straight path. It is specific commentary on all of canonical 1:6.
evidence.translation_alignment: Both complete translations retain every lexical sense and Qur'anic witness, the alternative concerning the female, full transmitted report, other Book/Islam reports, and both final Jarir lines. No verse association change arises in either language.
evidence.excluded_as_extra_targets: Retrieved and read full canonical 38:22, 41:17, 20:50 and 13:7. They occur as short lexical witnesses for hadā = guide, make clear, inspire and call; even the brief glosses of 20:50 and 13:7 remain part of this dictionary-like comparison, closed by وأصل هذا كله أرشد. They are illustrative cross-references, not separately developed explanations requiring mappings. The poem is likewise a lexical witness for sirat.
